name: The Sadhu
summary: A Virgin Comics series from 2006 about a British soldier in colonial India who trains under mystics and returns with reality-bending powers to confront the man who wronged him.
origin: Created by Gotham Chopra with artist Jeevan Kang, The Sadhu was one of the first titles in Virgin Comics' Shakti line, which mixed Indian themes with modern comics. James Jensen, a British soldier in the Bengal of the East India Company era, is wronged by a brutal colonel. Rescued by a shaman and trained in reality-shaping powers, he becomes a sadhu seeking justice. It is a mature revenge story, best for older readers.
creators: Jeevan Kang (artist and cover artist, co-creator)
powers: Reality-bending powers learned from a shaman
A forehead energy wave, borrowing the image of a third eye
Training in the mystic practices of sadhus
Reincarnated knowledge of a past sage

storyline.title: A soldier in Bengal
storyline.beat: James Jensen joins the British Indian Army after his wife becomes pregnant, then suffers a terrible loss at the hands of the ruthless Colonel Townsend and escapes into the jungle. Sources differ on his son: Wikipedia's plot says the boy died, while The Silent Ones has Jack held captive.

storyline.title: Dada Thakur
storyline.beat: After James flees the army camp with a fellow soldier's help, a jungle shaman, once the student of Jensen's past self, saves him in the jungle and trains him for three years in powers that bend reality.

storyline.title: Townsend as a demon sadhu
storyline.beat: Jensen goes after Townsend, who in the comic prays to the destructive side of the goddess Kali, becomes a demon sadhu and builds power in London's underworld.

storyline.title: When Realities Collide
storyline.beat: The opening arc is collected in a 196-page paperback in July 2007.

storyline.title: The Silent Ones
storyline.beat: A five-issue miniseries by Saurav Mohapatra sends James searching for his captive son Jack, against a cult and its Grand Mistress.

storyline.title: Warrior: Revenge of the Sadhu
storyline.beat: Producer Mark Canton and Graphic India develop a film version under the working title Warrior: Revenge of the Sadhu.

gossip.text: Gotham Chopra, who created the series, is the son of author Deepak Chopra, who wrote notes at the end of each issue.
In 2006 Variety reported that Nicolas Cage was set to star in a film version, with Deepak Chopra writing the script. It never reached cameras.
Critics compared the comic's surreal art and Hindu mythology to Neil Gaiman's Sandman.
A 2014 film writer hired for the project, Mukunda Michael Dewil, once quit an advertising job in Cape Town to live with sadhus in Vrindavan.
Some think The Sadhu is an ancient mythological tale.
gossip.truth: It is a 2006 original comic that borrows ideas from Hindu thought.

quiz.q: Which publisher launched The Sadhu in 2006?
quiz.why: It was a Shakti-line title from Virgin Comics, backed by Richard Branson.

quiz.q: For how many years does the shaman Dada Thakur train James Jensen?
quiz.why: Dada Thakur trains him for three years in powers that bend reality.

quiz.q: Which producer of the film 300 developed a Sadhu film in 2014?
quiz.why: Mark Canton and Graphic India announced a film adaptation.

theme.tagline: Open the inner eye, find the way.

facts.text: Virgin planned much of its art in a Bangalore studio, where many artists had started as street painters and temple painters.
Variety reported that Nicolas Cage would headline a film version with Deepak Chopra as screenwriter, but no film was made.
Screenwriter Mukunda Michael Dewil, hired in June 2014, had left an ad job in Cape Town to live with sadhus in Vrindavan.
Buried alive, James escapes with a fellow soldier's help; later in the jungle Dada Thakur uses reality-bending power to shrink him to the size of an atom.
The powers James learns include great speed, phasing through matter, combat skills and manipulating time.
A feature on Graphic India describes the hero's new ability as a Shiva-like wave of energy sent through a third eye on his forehead, an image borrowed from Hindu iconography.
Dada Thakur drives off a unit of British soldiers by freezing their bullets in mid-air and sending a wave of energy from his forehead.
Dada Thakur teaches that reality is a matter of perception, so by changing how his mind sees the world James can change the world itself.
James shows a doubting English professor of occult studies that he can fly, then asks him about a 'demon sadhu' he believes is loose in the country.
The Sadhu's India is split between British troops with their landowner allies, the zamindars, and bands of Robin Hood-like bandits called dakaits, whom the shaman Dada Thakur leads.
James's younger brother William works the London docks beside him, stays behind when James sails east, and ends up running an inn under Colonel Townsend's control.
James is impressed when Dada Thakur heals a wounded boy, and soon afterwards asks the shaman to train him in the same arts.
After James's first duel with the demon sadhu Townsend goes badly for lack of experience, the English professor's daughter, who knows about his powers, nurses him back to health.
The tale has a third part, The Wheel of Destiny, a second five-issue miniseries after The Silent Ones.
The Silent Ones was written by Saurav Mohapatra and edited by Ron Marz, and picks up straight after the end of issue 8 of the main series.
In August 2010 Liquid Comics, successor to Virgin, put all five issues of The Silent Ones online free on Scribd.
Townsend's bosses tell him India is a key opium-producing region the East India Company wants firmly secured, since the drug is sold to China, which sets the story in real colonial history.
Dada Thakur has James attacked with sticks and bullets to test him, and James's unconscious mystical powers awaken and shield him.
After three years of training James quits abruptly, because his urge for revenge against Townsend grows too strong to control.
The opening arc's first four issues ran from July to October 2006, then a gap followed before issue 5 in February 2007 and issue 6 in March.
In the comic's own story the sadhu is a force for good recruited by a goddess, and James's whole life is framed as preparation for that role.

kidSummary: The Sadhu is a mature 2006 comic for older readers, so ask a grown-up first. A British soldier in colonial India suffers a great loss, learns reality-bending skills from a shaman, and discovers that letting go is the heart of a sadhu's path.

story.title: A soldier in Bengal
story.text: James Jensen, a dock worker from London, joins the British army and sails to India. There he stumbles on a temple and feels his destiny is tied to this land.

story.title: A shaman's rescue
story.text: After clashing with a cruel colonel, James escapes into the jungle with a soldier's help. The shaman Dada Thakur saves him and says James was once his own teacher.

story.title: Reality is perception
story.text: For three years Dada Thakur trains him in speed, phasing and time tricks, and teaches that changing how the mind sees the world can change the world.

story.title: The demon sadhu
story.text: The colonel has turned to the dark side of Kali and become a demon sadhu with power in London. James sets out to face him.

story.title: The search goes on
story.text: In a later miniseries, The Silent Ones, James looks for his son Jack with the help of a mad sadhu named Trishanku.
